newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK's Brown argues fuel VAT cut is legal.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown argues fuel VAT cut is legal.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown held discussions with top European Commission officials early on Monday to argue his planned cut in value added tax (VAT) on domestic fuel consumption was legal.

A Treasury official said Brown was telling the European Commissioner Mario Monti and Yves Thibault de Siguy, European Commissioner responsible for monetary affairs, that Labour would cut VAT on fuel to five percent from eight percent.
"He's telling them that the cut in VAT on fuel is legally water-tight," the official said.
Brown is in Brussels for his first meeting of EU finance ministers.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said he expected a more "open minded" approach from Britian in the run-up to June's inter-governmental conference.
